import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

# Source file paths
source0_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_95/training_0.csv"
source1_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_95/training_1.csv"

# Load source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the first numerical index column
df_source0 = pd.read_csv(source0_path, index_col=0)
df_source1 = pd.read_csv(source1_path, index_col=0)

# --- Understanding source schemas and target schema ---
# Source0 columns: ['School ID', 'name', 'type', 'size', 'budget']
# Source1 columns: ['Student ID', 'name', 'gender', 'grade', 'school', 'reading_score', 'math_score']
# Target columns: ['School Name', 'Student Grade', 'School ID', 'School Size', 'School Budget',
#                  'Student ID', 'Student Reading Score', 'Average Student Math Score']

# Transformation plan:
# 1. Source0 contains school-level info: School ID, name (school name), type, size, budget
# 2. Source1 contains student-level info: Student ID, name (student name), gender, grade, school (school name), reading_score, math_score
# 3. Target requires:
#    - School Name (string) -> from Source0.name or Source1.school (should be consistent)
#    - Student Grade (string) -> from Source1.grade
#    - School ID (int) -> from Source0.School ID
#    - School Size (int) -> from Source0.size
#    - School Budget (int) -> from Source0.budget
#    - Student ID (float) -> from Source1.Student ID (cast to float)
#    - Student Reading Score (float) -> from Source1.reading_score (cast to float)
#    - Average Student Math Score (float) -> from Source1.math_score (cast to float)
#
# 4. Join Source1 (student-level) with Source0 (school-level) on school name to get school info for each student.
#    Note: Source0.name and Source1.school are the join keys.
#
# 5. After join, rename columns to target schema names.
#
# 6. Cast columns to required types.
#
# 7. Save to target CSV.

# --- Data cleaning and preparation ---

# Check for consistent school name formats between Source0 and Source1
# To be safe, strip whitespace and lowercase for join keys
df_source0['school_name_key'] = df_source0['name'].str.strip().str.lower()
df_source1['school_name_key'] = df_source1['school'].str.strip().str.lower()

# Join Source1 with Source0 on school_name_key to get school info for each student
df_merged = pd.merge(
    df_source1,
    df_source0[['School ID', 'school_name_key', 'size', 'budget']],
    on='school_name_key',
    how='inner',
    validate='many_to_one'  # many students to one school
)

# After join, build the target dataframe with required columns and names

# Map columns:
# 'School Name' <- from Source0.name (we can get it from df_source0 by matching school_name_key)
# Since we have school_name_key in merged, get original school name from Source0 by mapping
school_name_map = df_source0.set_index('school_name_key')['name']
df_merged['School Name'] = df_merged['school_name_key'].map(school_name_map)

# 'Student Grade' <- df_merged['grade']
# 'School ID' <- df_merged['School ID']
# 'School Size' <- df_merged['size']
# 'School Budget' <- df_merged['budget']
# 'Student ID' <- df_merged['Student ID']
# 'Student Reading Score' <- df_merged['reading_score']
# 'Average Student Math Score' <- df_merged['math_score']

# Construct final dataframe with target schema column order
df_target = pd.DataFrame({
    'School Name': df_merged['School Name'],
    'Student Grade': df_merged['grade'],
    'School ID': df_merged['School ID'],
    'School Size': df_merged['size'],
    'School Budget': df_merged['budget'],
    'Student ID': df_merged['Student ID'],
    'Student Reading Score': df_merged['reading_score'],
    'Average Student Math Score': df_merged['math_score']
})

# Cast columns to target types
df_target['School Name'] = df_target['School Name'].astype(str)
df_target['Student Grade'] = df_target['Student Grade'].astype(str)
df_target['School ID'] = df_target['School ID'].astype(int)
df_target['School Size'] = df_target['School Size'].astype(int)
df_target['School Budget'] = df_target['School Budget'].astype(int)
df_target['Student ID'] = df_target['Student ID'].astype(float)
df_target['Student Reading Score'] = df_target['Student Reading Score'].astype(float)
df_target['Average Student Math Score'] = df_target['Average Student Math Score'].astype(float)

# Save to target CSV
target_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_95/target_multisource_cot.csv"
df_target.to_csv(target_path, index=False)

import pandas as pd

# Read source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the first numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_95/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_95/training_1.csv", index_col=0)

# Join Source1 (students) with Source0 (schools) on school name
df = pd.merge(source1, source0, left_on="school", right_on="name", how="inner")

# Rename columns to match target schema
df = df.rename(columns={
    "name_y": "School Name",
    "grade": "Student Grade",
    "School ID": "School ID",
    "size": "School Size",
    "budget": "School Budget",
    "Student ID": "Student ID",
    "reading_score": "Student Reading Score",
    "math_score": "math_score"
})

# Select and reorder columns to match target schema before aggregation
df = df[[
    "School Name",
    "Student Grade",
    "School ID",
    "School Size",
    "School Budget",
    "Student ID",
    "Student Reading Score",
    "math_score"
]]

# Group by leftmost non-float columns in target schema
group_cols = ["School Name", "Student Grade", "School ID", "School Size", "School Budget"]

# Aggregate Student ID and Student Reading Score by mean, math_score by mean renamed to Average Student Math Score
agg_df = df.groupby(group_cols).agg({
    "Student ID": "mean",
    "Student Reading Score": "mean",
    "math_score": "mean"
}).reset_index()

# Rename math_score to Average Student Math Score
agg_df = agg_df.rename(columns={"math_score": "Average Student Math Score"})

# Write output to target file
agg_df.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_95/target_multisource_critique_history.csv", index=False)
